name_note: The GTDB genus Merdibacter also holds genomes deposited as Solobacterium, and its representative genome is labelled Candidatus Merdibacter merdavium, a different species from the Merdibacter massiliensis described here.

sentences.text: The genus Merdibacter was proposed for strain Marseille-P3254, isolated from an ileal sample of a 76-year-old woman who underwent upper and lower digestive tract endoscopy.
It was described as an anaerobic Gram-negative bacterium without catalase and oxidase activities, representing a novel genus within the family Erysipelotrichaceae in the phylum Firmicutes.
Its genome was reported as 2,468,496 bp with 40.1 percent G+C content, most closely related to Eubacterium dolichum, sharing 90.7 percent 16S rRNA sequence similarity.
A 16S study of patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease reported higher abundance of Merdibacter in the group without intracranial aneurysms.
